 WATCH: Leaked video shows Senatobia police shooting that killed 1-year-old Kohen Wiley 
 By Hannah Kozlowski and Michaela Redmond Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 11:55 AM CDT | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SENATOBIA, Miss. (WMC) - Action News 5 has obtained footage showing the Senatobia police shooting that killed 1-year-old Kohen Wiley on June 14.
 This undated photo provided by Veronica Roberson in June 2026 shows her grandson, Kohen Wiley, of Senatobia, Miss. (Veronica Roberson | Veronica Roberson via AP) Action News 5 received the footage from Darkhorse Press two days after Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch’s office determined the officers’ actions that day were justified .
 The obtained footage includes five videos: three body-camera videos from Senatobia officers and two surveillance videos from Walmart.
 According to Darkhorse Press, Senatobia police were called to Walmart that day after a complaint about a “pervert” was made, unrelated to the two women Wiley was with who were accused of shoplifting.
 One video shows the store’s security guard talking to Kohen’s mother, Vellesiya Wiley, and his great-aunt. Moments later, video shows Wiley, who was holding Kohen, and the other woman running to a car. The woman gets in the driver’s seat and Wiley gets in the front passenger seat with Kohen.
 Another video shows law enforcement officers in the store’s loss prevention office being interrupted by a store employee saying “two women are running.” Moments later, video shows law enforcement officers running after Wiley and the other woman as both get into the car.
 Officers are then seen in front of the car as the driver backs out of the parking spot. Officers can be heard telling the driver to stop with guns drawn.
 The driver is then seen driving toward officers, hitting one and crossing into the next parking lot aisle, striking a parked vehicle and later driving off.
 It is unclear from the videos provided which officers fired their weapons, and which shots struck Wiley. Action News 5 does not have body-camera video from the officer who was hit by the vehicle.
 The final body-camera video shows officers outside an emergency medical center, where an unidentified officer said, “I didn’t even see a f—ing baby in her lap.”
 “Nobody knew the baby was there,” another officer said. “All I saw was two females in the car.”
 Patrick Lumumba, the founder of the Senatobia Committee for Accountability and Transparency, said the community is still hurting. Lumumba said he is especially hurting after watching the leaked footage. 
 “You didn’t know there was an f-ing baby in the car? You know what I’m saying and, or, did your testosterone just drive you to shoot into this car and then once you realized you shot and killed a baby now you don’t know there was an f-ing baby in the car. So, this community is still hurting,” said Lumumba. 
 Lumumba said SCAT remains focused on seeking justice for Wiley. He added there should never have been shots fired in the Walmart parking lot and the footage proved that. 
 “Especially after seeing how this all actually played out because there were false narratives that were presented by the city saying that they saw women running to a car fleeing to a car,” said Lumumba. “From the video I saw, you couldn’t have possibly seen it. You were informed that somebody was running and you got out of your position and ran after somebody that was running...and this is where these shots were fired.” 
 Lumumba said it looks like the Senatobia Police Officer took a deliberate position in front of the car to fire his weapon. After the officer moves around the car, Lumumba said the video shows him directly fire into the vehicle. 
 Lumumba questioned Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch’s decision that Foster’s actions were justified saying the case should have been sent to a grand jury. 
 “I’m trying to see how that’s justifiable when you got a whole city that’s in diametric opposition, a whole city that’s having different viewpoints about what took place on June the 14 th . So, how can you Lynn Fitch make a unilateral decision,” said Lumumba. 
 The footage appears to contradict parts of Vellesiya Wiley’s previous account . In a June 17 video statement released through attorneys Ben Crump and Van Turner, Wiley said she continued walking “because it had nothing to do with me” after officers stopped her friend, and said her friend drove toward the other side of the lot, away from officers. The leaked video shows both women running to the car, and the car driving toward officers and hitting one.
 Wiley also said she lifted Kohen up “trying to show them that he was in the car” after seeing officers draw their guns.
 Background: 
 On June 14, Senatobia police responded to an alleged shoplifting involving diapers at Walmart. Wiley was inside a car with his mother, who was holding him, and his great-aunt, who was driving.
 According to the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation, the driver drove toward officers and nearly struck one of them. An officer then fired toward the vehicle, striking Wiley and the driver. Wiley died from his injuries.
 MBI assigned five agents to the case. Investigators reviewed witness statements, body- and dash-camera video and Walmart surveillance video.
 The officer who fired was placed on administrative leave, which city leaders said is standard practice after deadly police shootings.
 In July , Wiley’s cause of death was ruled a homicide, according to an independent autopsy report requested by the family.
 Van Turner along with civil rights attorney Ben Crump are representing Wiley’s family. They have renewed calls for MBI and Walmart to release all surveillance video from the incident.
 Action News 5 has reached out to the Mississippi Department of Public Safety about the leaked video and whether there are plans to release the video independently. DPS said it still plans to sit down with the Wiley family this week and then release it.
 Action News 5 also reached out to family attorneys Ben Crump and Van Turner. Turner told Action News 5 they were aware of the video and plan to meet with the family Thursday to review the video themselves.
 This story will be updated as more information is released.
